method: Read-only diff and existing protocol/handler/initialization API trace; no build or runtime execution.
conclusion: No blocking source defect found in this minimal dispatch repair. Actual app-server public JSON-RPC tests remain required.
findings: Existing protocol declares both methods experimental. The initialized-client dispatch rejects absent opt-in before queueing or invoking the account handler.
Existing serialization scopes remain global_shared_read(account-auth) for discover and global(account-auth) for setup.
The new branches only route the already defined parameters to their existing handlers; handler result types match the shared response chain.
Existing workload identity, external ChatGPT auth, forced login, higher-precedence provider, supported-region and credential conflict checks remain in the reached handlers.

Discovery response contains profile names, credential kinds and regions, not secret values. Setup validates available credential selection but does not perform Bedrock service authorization verification.
The old dead_code expectations no longer describe reachable methods and are removed without deleting the methods.
The original three public positive/conflict tests are retained. The appended stable-client regression exercises actual JSON-RPC rejection for both methods and asserts no config/auth/.env write.
The regression uses existing TestAppServer builder and initialize_with_capabilities API; README scope matches the actual handler rather than claiming a remote Bedrock permission check.
limits: Static review does not establish Rust compilation or test success.
Existing profile credential loading may use its provider chain; this review does not claim all credential resolution is network-free.
